<x_0.0225><y_0.0266>of the atmosphere and in the mine to produce the ne-
ceffary circulation. This happens principally in the
fpring and autumn; at which feafons it is neceflary to
light fires in the thafts, which are always efficacious for
the purposfe defined.<x_0.8311><y_0.0969><class_Text>

<x_0.8428><y_0.0273>Damfel
II Danze.<x_0.9658><y_0.0688><class_Picture>

<x_0.0215><y_0.0961>Among the other ufcs to which dephlogificated air
might be applied, Mr Cavallo reckons that of fecuring
people from the dangerous effects of damps in mines,
and other fubterraneous places. " If a large blad-
der," fays he, " into which a folution of lime in wa-
ter is introduced, be filled with dephlogificated air,
and a fmall wooden or glafs pipe be adapted to its
neck, a man may hold that pipe in his mouth, and
may breathe the dephlogiflicted air; and thus equip-
ped he may enter into thefe fubterranean places,
amidft the various clafic fluids contained in them.
A large bladder of dephlogificated air will ferve
for above a quarter of an hour, which is a length of
time sufficient for various purposes; belides, if longer
time is required to be fpent in thefe places, a per-
fon may have two or more bladders of dephlogificated
air along with him, and may shift as foon as the air of
one is contaminated. Without the necessity of any
more complicated apparatus, the bladders full of de-
phlogificated air may be kept flopped by putting corks
into the glafs or wooden pipes that are tied to their
neeks. This air might alfo be ufed for diving-bells."<x_0.832><y_0.4><class_Text>

<x_0.0195><y_0.3992>DAMSEL, from the French _danoifel_ or _dansifeau_,
an appellation anciently given to all young people of
either fex, that were of noble or genteel extraction, as
the fons and daughters of princes, knights, and barons:
thus we read of Damfel Pepin, Damfel Louis le Gros,
Damfel Richard prince of Wales.<x_0.8281><y_0.482><class_Text>

<x_0.0205><y_0.4828>From the fons of kings this appellation frift paffed
to thofe of great lords and barons, and at length to
thofe of gentlemen who were not yet knights.<x_0.8262><y_0.5242><class_Text>

<x_0.0176><y_0.5234>At present damfel is applied to all maids or girls not
yet married, provided they be not of the vulgar.<x_0.8242><y_0.5508><class_Text>

<x_0.0166><y_0.5516>DAN, or JOR-DAN, which laft literally denotes " the
river Dan;" fo named from the people where it has
its fource, which is a lake called _Phiala_, from its round
figure, to the north of its apparent rifing from the
mountain Panium or Paneum, as was difcovered by
Philip, Tetrarch of Trachonites; for on throwing light
bodies into the Phiala, he found them to emerge again
at Paneum (Jofephus). From Paneum it runs in a
direct courte to a lake called _Samachonites_; as far as
which it is called _Yordan the Left_; and thence to the
lake Gencfareth, or of Tiberias, where it comes in-
creafed by the lake Samachonitis and its springs, and
is called the _Greater Jordan_; continuing its direct
courfe fourthwards, till it falls into the Afphaltites.<x_0.8252><y_0.743><class_Text>

<x_0.0156><y_0.7438>DAN (anc. geog.), a town to the welt of the fource
of the Jordan; formerly called _Laii_ (Jofhua, Judges,
Jofephus). This was the north, as Beerheba was the
fourth, boundary of the Ifraclites; as appears from the
common expreflion in Scripture, from _Dan_ to _BeerIbe-
ba._ At Dan Jeroboam erected one of the golden
calves (1 Kings xii.).<x_0.8203><y_0.8398><class_Text>

<x_0.0146><y_0.8391>DAN, the tribe, extended itself weftward of Judah,
and was terminated by Azotus and Dora on the Medi-
terranean (Jofepkus).<x_0.8184><y_0.882><class_Text>

<x_0.0137><y_0.8805>DANAE, in antiquity, a coin fomewhat more than
an obolus, ufed to be put into the mouths of the dead,
to pay their paffage over the river Acheron.<x_0.8193><y_0.9242><class_Text>

<x_0.6836><y_0.9211>DANAE,<x_0.8213><y_0.9367><class_Text>
